дивитися.text: Originally meant "to marvel (at)", compare with Russian диви́ться (divítʹsja). The meaning "to watch", "to look (at)" developed later. Compare also with Czech dívat se.

sources.quote: Univerbation of май (maj) + же (že), the imperative singular of ма́ти (máty, “to consider”). Compare Russian почти́, счита́й (počtí, sčitáj) and Polish prawie że.

sources.quote: From Proto-Slavic *berzьnь (“March; April”), from *berza (“birch”) + *-ьnъ. Related to бере́за (beréza), referring to birch trees which bloom at this time of year, with -ень (-enʹ). Cognates include Polish brzezień (“March”), Czech březen, Russian березозол (berezozol), and Bulgarian брезен (brezen…

березень.text: From Proto-Slavic *berzьnь (“March; April”), from *berza (“birch”) + *-ьnъ. Related to бере́за (beréza), referring to birch trees which bloom at this time of year, with -ень (-enʹ). Cognates include Polish brzezień (“March”), Czech březen, Russian березозол (berezozol), and Bulgarian брезен (brezen, “April”).
